subject: literature
passage: Helena had been standing under the arrivals board for an hour, her coat buttoned to the chin. Every few minutes she looked up at the board, though only one train from the north was due that evening, and its time had not changed. When the train was finally announced, she pressed forward to the barrier before the first passengers had even stepped down, searching each face. The last to come through was a young woman with a battered suitcase, and Helena's hands went to her mouth. The way Helena waited suggests that ______
stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: she had come to the station to catch a train herself.
choices.B: she did not know which train the young woman would be on.
choices.C: she was anxious to meet someone whose arrival mattered greatly to her.
choices.D: she was worried that the train would be canceled because of the weather.

explanation.why: Helena watches the board constantly even though nothing changes, rushes to the barrier before anyone gets off, and studies every face. Her reaction when the young woman appears confirms that she was waiting for a particular person who was very important to her.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Helena waits at the arrivals board and the barrier, watching passengers come through, not departing herself.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The text says only one train from the north was due, so Helena knew which train to watch for.
explanation.C: Correct. Her constant checking, eager rush to the barrier, and emotional reaction show she was anxiously awaiting someone important.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text mentions neither weather nor any fear that the train would be canceled.
